name: Our Tanya is Crying Out Loud
description: Right now she actually isn't. But she will be, if you don't solve this problem. You are given integers n , k , A and B . There is a number x , which is initially equal to n . You are allowed to perform two types of operations: Subtract 1 from x . This operation costs you A coins. Divide x by k . Can be performed only if x is divisible by k . This operation costs you B coins. What is the minimum amount of coins you have to pay to make x equal to 1 ?
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer n ( 1 ≤ n ≤ 2·10 9 ). The second line contains a single integer k ( 1 ≤ k ≤ 2·10 9 ). The third line contains a single integer A ( 1 ≤ A ≤ 2·10 9 ). The fourth line contains a single integer B ( 1 ≤ B ≤ 2·10 9 ).
output_specification: Output a single integer — the minimum amount of coins you have to pay to make x equal to 1 .
approach_summary: Apply Knapsack and Basic Dynamic Programming paradigm under the Dynamic Programming (DP) framework. Exploit problem invariants to reduce state space and achieve optimal complexity.
